<explanation>
Based on the provided file tree and README content, you’re working with mPDF—a PHP library designed to generate PDF files from UTF-8 encoded HTML. mPDF encapsulates many PDF-generation features (like barcode support, CSS and HTML parsing, font handling, and more) in a modular design. Below is a detailed guide on how to draw a system design diagram that accurately reflects the mPDF architecture.

1. Identify the Main Components:
   • Mpdf API (the Public Interface): This is the primary entry point (the Mpdf class) that developers work with. It accepts configuration parameters and serves as the orchestrator.
   • HTML/CSS Parsing & Tag System: Located in sections such as src/Tag and src/Css, this component handles the interpretation of HTML elements, applying CSS rules, and converting them into PDF constructs.
   • PDF Generation Engine: Comprising the Writer submodules (under src/Writer) and the classes in src/Pdf, this part builds the actual PDF – placing objects, pages, and resources accordingly.
   • Asset & Resource Management: With modules such as src/AssetFetcher, src/File, and src/Fonts, this handles retrieving external resources (such as images, fonts, and assets) and managing the associated configurations.
   • Utility & Helper Modules: These include components in src/Utils, src/Cache, src/Color, src/Conversion, and parts of src/Container. They support tasks such as color conversion, barcode creation, and caching of fonts.
   • External Services and Dependencies: Although mPDF is a library, it integrates external HTTP clients (src/Http) to fetch assets, and has dependencies on PHP extensions (mbstring, gd, etc.), as well as using Composer for package management.
   • Testing and Supporting Boilerplate: The tests folder and utils directories provide unit tests and auxiliary tools for development, quality assurance, and maintenance.

2. Define Relationships and Interactions:
   • At the top, the Mpdf API initializes the configuration (from src/Config) and drives the overall process.
   • The API delegates HTML to CSS parsing to the Tag system and CSS Manager. The parsed elements are then mapped to corresponding PDF objects.
   • The PDF Generation Engine (with Writers and Pdf classes) compiles these objects and interacts with lower-level utilities (font handling, color management, image processing) to render the final output.
   • Asset Fetchers, HTTP Clients, and File Loaders support the inclusion of external media – these modules work in tandem with the main engine to supply required data.
   • The Barcode module and Conversion components provide additional functionality for features like barcodes, converting numeric data, or adjusting layouts.
   • Utility classes and containers glue together these components and make error handling (via Exception classes) and logging (src/Log) consistent throughout the system.

3. Highlight Architectural Patterns and Technical Features:
   • Modularization: mPDF is built as a collection of loosely coupled components that interact through clearly defined interfaces.
   • Separation of Concerns: Each feature – whether it’s asset fetching, PDF generation, or tag processing – is encapsulated in its own module.
   • Dependency Injection & Container Pattern: The Container (src/Container) is used for managing dependencies, allowing for easier testing and maintenance.
   • Extension and Configuration: The extensive use of configuration files (like composer.json, configuration directives in the README) indicates that customization is supported via dependency configuration.

4. Guidelines Specific to This Project:
   – Since mPDF is a library rather than a complete full-stack application, your diagram should emphasize modular design over traditional frontend-backend separation.
   – Begin by drawing a top-level block labeled “Mpdf API” (or “Mpdf Gateway”) from which arrows lead down to the main modules (HTML/CSS Parser, PDF Engine, Asset Management, etc.).
   – Include a separate section for “Utilities & Helpers,” showing components such as Color Conversion, Barcode, File I/O, and Container/Dependency Injection.
   – As mPDF integrates multiple subdirectories (like src/Tag, src/Writer, src/Pdf, etc.) that cooperate to build PDFs, represent these as clusters of components grouped by functionality.
   – Although not a network service, showing interactions (dashed arrows) to external libraries/HTTP clients and PHP extensions (mbstring, gd, etc.) will be helpful.

5. Diagram Elements and Visual Guidelines:
   • Use clear labels for each component (e.g., “Mpdf API,” “HTML Parser & Tag Manager,” “PDF Writer,” “Asset & Font Manager,” “HTTP Client,” “Utility Modules”).
   • Utilize directional arrows to show data flow and control: for instance, from the Mpdf API to the Tag Parser to the PDF Writer.
   • Different colors or shapes can be used to differentiate between core library modules (perhaps a solid box) and supporting utilities (maybe rounded boxes). For example, use a unique color for modules handling external dependencies (HTTP client, file loader).
   • Include annotations (or sub-text) to indicate key responsibilities, such as “Handles barcode generation” for the Barcode module or “Manages font caching” for the FontCache in src/Fonts.

6. Bringing It All Together:
   – Start your diagram from a “Client Code” block that initializes the Mpdf object.
   – The Mpdf block then connects downward to two broad components: one handling parsing (HTML/CSS, Tag interpretation, Conversion) and one handling PDF generation (Page Writing, Resource Management).
   – Show supporting modules (Asset Fetcher, HTTP Module, Container, Exceptions) interacting with both the main parsing and PDF generation engines.
   – Optionally, a separate note or module can indicate external testing tools and Composer integration, though these are more for development and less for runtime interactions.

By following these guidelines and accurately mapping each segment of the file tree to a functional module, you can create a detailed and informative architecture diagram that reflects mPDF’s inner workings. This detailed representation will help any engineer understand the various components, their responsibilities, and how they cooperate to convert HTML/CSS into a PDF document.
</explanation>
